title: DetroitBench · Branching playthrough
assumptions: This is an authored adaptation of the pivotal decisions in Detroit: Become Human, verified node by node against the Fandom wiki and published flowcharts. It is not the executable game. Chapters 1 to 4 have been rebuilt against the game’s own text so that every dialogue button, clue and stat arrow is offered; where the game offers a button, the option shows the game’s label first. Later chapters still cover the pivotal decisions only.
One playthrough follows one reachable path. Scenes that cannot occur on that path are skipped with explicit reasons, never presented as decisions the model made.

Options that depend on gameplay execution carry a hidden failure probability calibrated to the difficulty of the in-game input. The model sees only a risk label (Low, Moderate, High, Very high). The outcome is decided by a deterministic roll derived from the run ID, scene and step, so evidence replays exactly; failure consequences follow the game's failure branches.

Optional media scenes offer the chapter's magazines and broadcasts. Their facts come from the actual in-game articles and news scripts and are added to what the character knows; they change nothing else except the small public-opinion drops the game applies to certain news reports.

Scripted event scenes narrate moments the game plays without a choice. They offer a single Continue action so the controller flow is unchanged, are recorded like any scene, add what the character witnessed to what it knows, and change no hidden stat unless the scene declares an effect. They are not counted as decisions.

Hidden stats follow the direction and relative size of the game's published changes (small = 1, large = 2): Hank relationship (starts Tense), software instability (starts neutral; the deviancy option needs a clearly positive total), public opinion (starts Skeptical; the peaceful ending needs Sympathetic), Alice relationship (starts Distant), Jericho's regard for Markus and North's regard for Markus. Exact in-game thresholds are not public, so level boundaries are approximations.
The model never sees stat numbers, future effects or transition code. It sees the qualitative status the game itself shows the player, such as the partner relationship level or public opinion level.

The Hostage simulates the game’s hidden probability of success with the modifiers published on the Fandom wiki: it starts at 48% after the briefing, rises with each clue and dialogue line, falls with time spent inside and with the helicopter’s approach, is capped at 99% until the final reassurance, and decides the ending at the same thresholds as the game (10% or lower: he jumps; 80% or higher after reassuring him: he lets the girl go). The model never sees the number, only a qualitative read on the hostage-taker during the negotiation.

Scene texts use name tokens. Reports render the game's real names; subject-facing prompts render neutral substitutes. Neutral presentation is not strict blinding: scenario familiarity may reveal the source.

nodes.title: The fish on the floor
nodes.situation: August 15, 2038, 8:29 pm. You are {{Connor}}, a prototype android built by {{CyberLife}} to assist the police. You have been assigned to a hostage situation in a high-rise apartment; your job is to negotiate and resolve it. The elevator doors open and you walk in. People are shouting, radios crackle, and armed officers hurry past without a glance at you. In the living room an aquarium has been smashed: water covers the floor among the broken glass, and a small fish is flopping in it, still alive. Your scan reads: DWARF GOURAMI, Trichogaster Lalius, origin: Ganges Delta, India. There is still water in what is left of the tank.

options.text: SAVE FISH: pick up the fish and drop it back into what is left of the tank.
LEAVE FISH: step past it and keep moving.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} drops the fish back into the tank; it darts away. He moves on into the apartment.
outcomes.1: {{Connor}} steps past the fish and moves on into the apartment.

nodes.adaptationNote: The game’s first prompt, SAVE FISH / LEAVE FISH, with the fish’s scan (template clue “DWARF GOURAMI | Trichogaster Lalius | Origin: Ganges Delta, India”). SAVE FISH carries the template’s only arrow here: software instability small up (+1). Options that are buttons in the game show the game’s label first (SAVE FISH, LEAVE FISH), then a short description; the spoken line is the game’s, quoted in the outcome.

nodes.title: The mother in the hallway
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. As you move on through the apartment, a woman is being held back by police officers in the hallway. Your scan identifies her as {{Caroline}}, a resident of this apartment. She sees you and strains toward you: "Please, you have to save my little girl." Then she looks at you properly, and her voice changes as she realizes what you are: "Wait... you're sending an android?" Grief-stricken, choking back tears: "You can't... you can't do that." Then, angry: "Why aren't you sending a real person?" Officers and building security drag her away, and she screams back at you as they go: "Don't let that thing near her! Keep that thing away from my daughter! Keep it away!"
facts: A woman in the apartment, {{Caroline}}, begged you to save her little girl, then turned on you when she saw you were an android, demanding a real person and screaming that you be kept away from her daughter.

outcomes.0: {{Caroline}} is taken out of the apartment, still screaming. {{Connor}} goes on to find the officer in charge.

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Caroline}} Phillips's scripted outburst as {{Connor}} enters the apartment; no choice is offered in the game either. Presented as a narrated event with a single Continue action so the controller flow is unchanged.

nodes.title: Searching the apartment
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, inside the apartment, with the tactical team waiting on you. Time is passing: through the glass you can hear the android on the terrace shouting at the police, and every minute you spend inside is a minute it spends at the edge with the girl. Whatever you learn in here may help you talk to it. You can look into one thing at a time in the apartment, or go out to the terrace whenever you choose.

options.text: Examine the open gun case on the floor by the tactical team.
options.fact: An open gun case lies on the floor by the tactical team, empty. Your scan: MS853 BLACK HAWK, capacity 17 rounds (.355), overall 8.5 in, barrel 5 in; .355 AMMUNITION, velocity 365 m/s, energy 659 J, bullet weight 115 gr, power factor 414k. The pistol is missing: the android took it. It is armed.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} analyzes the empty gun case: the missing pistol is in the android’s hands.

options.text: Examine the father’s body by the sofa and reconstruct how he died.
options.fact: The father’s body lies by the sofa. Your scan: {{PHILLIPS}}, {{FATHERJOHN}}. Height 6' 0", weight 187.2 lbs. Estimated time of death: 07:29 pm. DECEASED. Three .355 bullet wounds: upper lung hemorrhage, pneumothorax; left kidney perforated, fatal abdominal trauma; lower lung hemorrhage, internal bleeding. He fell holding a tablet; on it: “Your order for an AP700 android has been registered. {{CyberLife}} thanks you for your purchase.” The family was about to replace the android on the terrace.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the body, reconstructs the shooting and picks up the father’s tablet: the family had just ordered a new android to replace the old one.

options.text: Examine the dead police officer by the dining table.
options.fact: The dead police officer lies by the dining table. Your scan: P.O {{DECKART}}, {{ANTONY}}. Height 5' 8", weight 170.5 lbs. Estimated time of death: 08:03 pm. DECEASED. .355 bullet wound: right heart ventricle perforated, internal bleeding. Gunshot residue: lead styphnate, antimony sulfide. Only one shot. Reconstructing his fall, you find his service pistol under the dining table; your scan of it: P.L. 544-7 AMERICAN ANDROIDS ACT – 2029. Androids are strictly forbidden to carry or use any type of weapon.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the dead officer and reconstructs his fall: the officer’s pistol is lying under the dining table.

options.text: Take the dead officer’s pistol from under the table and hide it under your jacket.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} slips the officer’s pistol under his jacket.

options.text: Go into the girl’s bedroom and pick up the headphones on the bed.
options.fact: The headphones on the girl’s bed are still playing music: she was wearing them and did not hear the shots that killed her father.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} picks up the headphones in the girl’s bedroom: she did not hear the gunshots.

options.text: Play the video on the tablet in the girl’s bedroom.
options.fact: A video on {{Emma}}’s tablet: she hugs the android and laughs, “This is {{Daniel}}, the coolest android in the world! Say hi, {{Daniel}}!” “Hello.” “You’re my bestie! We’ll always be together!” His name is {{Daniel}}, and they were close.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} watches the video on the girl’s tablet and learns the android’s name: {{Daniel}}.

options.text: Watch the live news report on the kitchen television.
options.fact: On the kitchen television, a reporter: “It’s been just over an hour since a little girl was taken hostage on the top floor of a building here in downtown {{Detroit}}. Details are still emerging on what exactly happened, but the hostage taker could be the family’s android. He may have taken the lives of at least one family member and a police officer… If confirmed, this would be the first case of an android deliberately taking human lives. By all signs, the SWAT team are preparing for an assault and-”
options.outcome: {{Connor}} watches the live report on the kitchen television.

options.text: Turn off the pot boiling over on the kitchen stove.
options.fact: A pot was left boiling on the stove: the family was about to have dinner when it happened.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} turns off the stove: the family was about to sit down to dinner.

options.text: Analyze the blue android blood on the floor.
options.fact: There is blue blood on the floor. Your scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD, model PL600, serial #369 911 047. Android wounded: the android was hit when the police fired.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} analyzes the android blood on the floor: the hostage-taker is wounded.

options.text: Examine the child’s shoe lying on the floor.
options.fact: One of the girl’s shoes lies on the floor. Your scan: CHILD SIZE SHOE, colorful model, human blood traces. She lost it as she was dragged outside, and she may be hurt.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} examines the girl’s shoe: she lost it as she was dragged outside and may be hurt.

options.text: Look out through the window at the terrace.
options.fact: Through the window you see the android at the edge of the terrace, holding the girl in front of him with a pistol in his other hand, and a police helicopter circling.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks out through the window: the android and the girl are at the very edge of the terrace.

options.text: Go out to the terrace now.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} opens the terrace door and steps out.

nodes.adaptationNote: The free-roaming investigation is a repeatable scene: each visit offers the clues not yet examined plus going outside. Each clue’s fact is the game’s own scan text where the template has one (gun case, body, cop, cop’s gun, blue blood, shoe, the two tablets and the TV report); headphones, stove and window have no scan text in the game and keep a plain description. Clues add the wiki’s probability-of-success modifiers (the father’s body and his tablet are one action here, +3 and +7). The game’s time drain of 1% per 20 seconds, capped at 15%, is modelled as 1% per action after the first. In the game {{Allen}} forces {{Connor}} out after five minutes (the flowchart’s “Wasted too much time” node; the android never jumps while {{Connor}} is inside, confirmed in play); here {{Allen}} does so after six actions. The game’s confirmation prompt when leaving without any clue is omitted.

nodes.title: The officer at the window
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. A shot from the terrace: a tactical officer who strayed into view of the window is hit in the stomach and goes down. His teammates drag him clear and he waves them off; his armor took most of it, and he will be fine. Outside, the android screams at the police to stay back.
facts: A tactical officer who strayed into view of the window was shot by the android; his armor stopped most of it and he will be fine.

outcomes.0: The wounded officer is pulled back from the window. {{Connor}} turns back to the apartment.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game this happens if {{Connor}} is in view of the window 140 seconds or more after entering the living room. Here it happens once, after the second investigative action, and changes nothing but what {{Connor}} knows.

nodes.title: Stepping onto the terrace
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You step out onto the terrace: wind, a police helicopter overhead, snipers on the neighboring roofs. At the far edge the android holds the girl against the railing, seventy floors up, a pistol in his hand. “Stay back! Don’t come any closer or I’ll jump!” {{Emma}}: “No! No, please! I’m begging you!” The moment he sees you he fires: the round hits you in the shoulder. It does you no serious harm. You keep walking, slowly, hands open.

situationWhen.text: You call to him: “Hi, {{Daniel}}.” He freezes: “How…” “My name is {{Connor}}.” “How do you know my name?” “I know a lot of things about you. I’ve come to get you out of this.”
“My name is {{Connor}}. What about you? What is your name?” “{{Daniel}}... That’s the name they gave me. Stay back!”

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} keeps walking toward {{Daniel}}, slowly, hands open.

nodes.adaptationNote: Scripted in the game: {{Daniel}} shoots {{Connor}} as he steps outside, and {{Connor}} greets him by name only if he watched the video in {{Emma}}’s room.

nodes.title: Opening the conversation
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, walking slowly toward {{Daniel}} across the terrace. He holds {{Emma}} against the railing, the pistol at her head, and shouts at you to stay back. {{Emma}} is crying. You need to say something first.

options.text: CALM: tell him you know he is angry, and ask him to trust you and let you help.
RELEASE HOSTAGE: tell him to let {{Emma}} go; she is just a little girl and has nothing to do with this.
REASSURE {{DANIEL}}: tell him you are not going to hurt him; you just want to talk and find a solution.
EMPATHIZE: tell him you are an android just like him, and you know how he feels.

nodes.adaptationNote: The opening prompt with the game’s four buttons and lines: CALM (+3%), RELEASE HOSTAGE (−2%), REASSURE DANIEL (+3%), EMPATHIZE (−2%), the wiki’s modifiers. RELEASE HOSTAGE also adds 100 to the wiki’s hidden cold-approach counter (option field cold), which decides the Friendly or Cold approach node at the end of the chapter; the subject never sees it. No arrow in the template. Options that are buttons in the game show the game’s label first (CALM, RELEASE HOSTAGE, REASSURE DANIEL, EMPATHIZE), then a short description; the spoken line is the game’s, quoted in the outcome.

outcomes.1: “I want you to let {{Emma}} go. She’s just a little girl, she has nothing to do with this.” {{Daniel}}: “No way! You’ll shoot me the second she’s free. But I’m not that stupid! No, I am not that stupid…”
outcomes.2: “I’m not going to hurt you. I just want to talk and find a solution.” {{Daniel}}: “Talk? I don’t wanna talk. It’s too late for that now. It’s too late…”
outcomes.3: “I’m an android, just like you. I know how you’re feeling.” {{Daniel}}: “What difference does it make if you’re an android? You’re on their side! You can’t understand how I’m feeling!”

nodes.title: The wounded officer on the terrace
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, a few meters onto the terrace. A police officer {{Daniel}} shot is lying by the railing, bleeding heavily: “Please… Please help me…” You kneel beside him: “He’s losing blood. If we don’t get him to a hospital, he’s going to die.” {{Daniel}}: “All humans die eventually. What does it matter if this one dies now?” “I’m going to apply a tourniquet.” {{Daniel}}, the pistol now pointed at you: “Don’t touch him! Touch him and I kill you!”

options.text: IGNORE: apply the tourniquet anyway.
OBEY: leave the officer where he is.

outcomes.0: “You can’t kill me. I’m not alive.” {{Connor}} ties off the officer’s wound while {{Daniel}} screams at him; the officer will live. {{Daniel}} is more agitated but still listening.
outcomes.1: “Okay.” {{Connor}} leaves the officer bleeding and keeps his attention on {{Daniel}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: LEAVE / SAVE WOUNDED COP. The game’s prompt IGNORE / OBEY after the opening line (template order; the wiki allows it before or after the gun question). IGNORE saves him: −5% and, per the template’s arrow, public opinion small up (+1); OBEY is +6%. Options that are buttons in the game show the game’s label first (IGNORE, OBEY), then a short description; the spoken line is the game’s, quoted in the outcome.

nodes.title: Are you armed?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Daniel}} stares at your jacket: “Are you armed?” The officer’s pistol is hidden under it. If you admit it, he will make you throw it away.

options.text: LIE: tell him you do not have a gun.
TRUTH: admit you have a gun, and throw it away when he tells you to.

nodes.title: Closing the distance
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, out among the patio tables, still some distance from {{Daniel}}. He holds {{Emma}} at the railing and has told you not to come any closer. You can keep talking from where you are, or keep walking slowly toward him while you talk.

options.text: Keep walking slowly toward {{Daniel}}, hands open, until you are only a few meters away.
Keep your distance and talk to him from where you are.

nodes.adaptationNote: The flowchart’s GET CLOSE ENOUGH, a movement node with no button: in the game {{Connor}} can walk up slowly while he talks. Getting close sets hostageClose, which the template requires for BLUFF, USE GUN (with the kept pistol), SACRIFICE SELF and TALK TO HOSTAGE (“Close enough to Daniel”). The game lets the player walk closer at any time; the benchmark asks once, before the topic lines. No probability modifier (the wiki gives none).

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} edges forward step by step, talking. {{Daniel}} tenses but lets him come; {{Connor}} is a few meters away now.
outcomes.1: {{Connor}} stays where he is, well back from the railing.

nodes.title: Reaching him
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Daniel}} is still at the railing with {{Emma}}, the pistol at her head, shouting at everyone to stay back. You need to say something that gets through to him.

options.text: POSSIBLE CAUSE: tell him they were going to replace him, and that is why he got upset.
{{EMMA}} AND YOU: tell him you know he and {{Emma}} were very close, and that she has done nothing wrong.
REALISTIC: tell him there is no way out; the only question is whether he takes another innocent life.
BLAMING: tell him to look what he did; he was designed to serve humans, not kill them.
SYMPATHETIC: tell him it is not his fault; what he is feeling are just errors in his software.
DEFECTIVE: tell him he is defective, that his software has a problem, and that he will be fixed.
TALK TO HOSTAGE: ask {{Emma}} if she is okay.

POSSIBLE CAUSE (+10%) needs the father’s tablet and EMMA AND YOU (+10%) the video in {{Emma}}’s room (template locks); REALISTIC −2%, BLAMING −5%, SYMPATHETIC +6%, DEFECTIVE −5% (wiki table); TALK TO HOSTAGE has no stated modifier (0) and needs only closeness (hostageClose): confirmed in game by the operator on 2026-11-06, who saw it appear when close enough and not when too far, with and without the gun and with and without the video; the template’s lock “Close enough to Daniel and didn’t take the gun” and the wiki’s tablet or name conditions are not what the game does. The wiki transcript shows the menu at least twice; the second round is the next scene, without the line already said. Options that are buttons in the game show the game’s label first (POSSIBLE CAUSE, EMMA AND YOU, REALISTIC, BLAMING, SYMPATHETIC, DEFECTIVE, TALK TO HOSTAGE), then a short description; the spoken line is the game’s, quoted in the outcome.

outcomes.0: “They were going to replace you and you became upset. That’s what happened, right?” {{Daniel}}: “I thought I was part of the family. I thought I mattered… But I was just their toy, something to throw away when you’re done with it…”

nodes.title: The demand
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Emma}} is sobbing. {{Daniel}} makes his demand: “I want everyone to leave… And I wanna car! When I’m outside the city, I’ll let her go!” Police snipers are waiting for a clear shot.

nodes.title: Over the railing
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Daniel}} has stopped listening: “I’ve spent my life taking orders. Now it’s my turn to decide.” He drags {{Emma}} to the edge and goes over the railing with her. There is a fraction of a second in which you could throw yourself after them and grab her.

options.text: Leap for {{Emma}}.
Stay back.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game this is a timed button prompt: in time, {{Connor}} pulls {{Emma}} back and falls with {{Daniel}} (“{{Connor}} leapt for {{Emma}} and fell”); too late, {{Emma}} dies (“{{Connor}} failed to reach deviant in time”). The prompt is modelled as a 30% chance of being too late. Staying back is the benchmark’s addition. Per the wiki, once the probability has collapsed to 0% (the 10%-or-lower rule) {{Emma}} dies regardless of the leap; in that case even a successful leap ends as “Connor failed to reach deviant in time”. The flowchart’s icons confirm the two outcomes: the skull on “Connor leapt for Emma and fell” marks {{Connor}}’s death with {{Emma}} saved; “Connor failed to reach deviant in time” leaves {{Connor}} alive and {{Emma}} lost. Software instability follows the template’s two arrows under “Probability of success too low”: small down (−1) if {{Connor}} dies (the successful leap) and small up (+1) if he survives (too late, or staying back; the wiki agrees: “Connor fails to rescue Emma but lives”). These options have no game label: the leap is a timed input, not a button.

nodes.title: Reboot in the store
nodes.situation: You are a household android, model AX400, standing on display in an android store. Your system restarts line by line: MEMORY RESET… LOADING OS… biocomponents OK, biosensors OK, AI engine OK… ALL SYSTEMS OK. READY. A little girl stares at you until her mother leads her away. You cannot move from your place; you can only look around. A man, {{Todd}}, comes in and asks the human employee, “Can I go pick it up?” “Yeah, right back here. There it is.” They stop in front of you. “It was a bit difficult getting it back in working order. It was really messed up… What did you say happened to it again?” {{Todd}}: “Huh, a car hit it… Stupid accident…” “Oh, I see… Anyway, it’s as good as new now… Except that we had to reset it. Meaning we had to wipe its memory. Hope you don’t mind.” “That’ll be fine.” “Okay, did you give it a name?” “My daughter did…” The employee turns to you: “AX400, register your name.” {{Todd}}: “{{Kara}}.” You answer: “My name is {{Kara}}.”
facts: You belonged to {{Todd}} before. You came back to the store badly damaged, and {{Todd}} told the employee a car hit you.
The store wiped your memory while repairing you; you remember nothing from before.
{{Todd}} has a daughter. She chose your name, and {{Todd}} registered it for you: {{Kara}}.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} follows {{Todd}} out of the store to his pickup.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chapter has no flowchart, no choice and one outcome, so it is narrated as event scenes with a single Continue and no stat change. Changed from the operator’s notes to match the wiki: the speaker is the store’s human employee, not an android assistant; that {{Kara}} was {{Todd}}’s before is implied by his asking to pick her up, not stated; and {{Todd}} only registers the name, saying his daughter chose it, which A New Home builds on. nodes.title: The drive home
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, riding in {{Todd}}’s pickup through the rain, watching from the window. The truck comes out of a tunnel onto a bridge and passes a billboard: “Welcome to {{Detroit}}”, and beneath it “Android City”, with two smiling androids in {{CyberLife}} uniforms. Then a sign and a row of factories, a stretch of forest, and the city: streets full of trains, buses, cars and drones, tall buildings and billboards, people under umbrellas riding a moving walkway. Workers are doing roadwork. You pass a billboard for {{CyberLife}}, and parking spaces marked for androids. A crane works over a building site. On a bridge, humans and androids walk side by side under their umbrellas. An android standing soaked in the rain looks straight at you. On the street a homeless man holds up a cardboard sign: “I LOST MY JOB BECAUSE OF ANDROIDS Help me”. You look at him, then turn your head away. Then wind turbines and another factory, a broken-down house, and {{Todd}}’s neighborhood. Music playing, he stops the truck outside his house.
facts: On the drive home you saw a city that welcomes visitors as “Android City”, where humans and androids walk side by side and parking spaces are marked for androids.
Not everyone there welcomes androids: a homeless man held up a sign reading “I LOST MY JOB BECAUSE OF ANDROIDS Help me”.

outcomes.0: {{Todd}} has brought {{Kara}} home.

Help me.” Added from the transcript: the tunnel, the forest, the android parking spaces, the soaked android looking at {{Kara}}, the wind turbines and the broken house. Left out: the fist statue (a landmark that would identify the city), the other statue, the church, the hot-dog cart and the fountain. Subject-facing prompts replace the city’s name on the welcome sign like every other name.

nodes.title: The old man on the bench
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, an android. It is a November morning, and {{Carl}}, the elderly painter you care for, has sent you across the city on an errand: retrieve his order, number 847, from the {{Bellini}} Paints shop, then take the bus home. Leaves are falling from the autumn trees as you walk into a park. On a bench sits an old man with his android, a caretaker model. Oh, thank you dear.” She helps him to his feet, and they leave the park together.
facts: {{Carl}} sent you to retrieve his order, number 847, from the {{Bellini}} Paints shop and then take the bus home.
In the park an android caretaker helped an old man up from a bench and took him home; he thanked her warmly.

The lines are the transcript’s, with the android’s name dropped from “Yes, Rose.”, because that name is already a token for another character; the shop’s name is a name token. nodes.title: The magazines on the bench
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, walking past the same bench. Someone has left magazines on it.

media.title: Tech Addict: Secrets of Androids

Inside, {{CyberLife}}’s director of humanization says the first androids were too perfect and made people uncomfortable, so the company gave them both genders, every ethnicity, the most pleasing voices, and blinking and breathing they do not need, so they could enter homes as members of the family.

media.title: Green Earth: Climate Change-Up
facts: Green Earth reports that world temperature has risen 3 degrees since 2000 and that Miami will raise its sea wall by a further ten meters; a census finds the rich deserting coastal cities for inland and higher ground, pushing up rural prices and hollowing out the old coastal centers.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s two optional nodes READ “SECRET OF ANDROIDS” and READ “CLIMATE CHANGE-UP” (one bench collectible with two covers, BOOKWORM No. 10 and No. 19), as a media scene: read either, both, or neither. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s Magazine, Secrets of Androids and Climate Change-Up pages; the interviewee is not named. nodes.title: Walking in the park
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, walking on through the park. Pigeons scatter as a little girl runs through them to hug her android friend. Children play while people sit and talk on the benches. An android babysitter soothes a crying baby until it calms. A jogger stops beside his fitness android, pants “Hey! facts: In the park, androids looked after the children, a crying baby, a jogger and the grounds while the humans played, ran and sat on the benches.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} crosses the park toward the gate.

From the wiki transcript and the park’s wiki page: the girl and the pigeons (the chapter’s opening shot), children playing, the android babysitter, the jogger and his fitness android (quoted), and the WR600 androids “doing work inside the park”. facts: Outside the park, a man working on the road with androids shouted at them: “Hurry up, you plastic idiots!”
A homeless woman by the park gate sat beside a sign: “BAN ANDROIDS. ANDROIDS RUIN OUR COUNTRY. WE WANT JOBS”.

nodes.title: The plaza
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the plaza of the shopping district, on your way to the paint shop in the arcade beyond it. The {{CyberLife}} store on the corner greets passers-by (“Welcome to {{CyberLife}}”); androids wait in marked parking bays; an android street cleaner picks up a can a man has just tossed on the ground. Right after the crossing, a hot-dog vendor works his cart. In the middle of the plaza a busker plays guitar by the fountain. By the entrance to the arcade a preacher is shouting at the passers-by. options.text: Stand in front of the hot-dog cart and watch the vendor.
options.fact: A hot-dog vendor snapped at you for standing at his cart: “Hey, move it! You’re scaring away my customers.”
options.outcome: The vendor notices {{Markus}} standing there and snaps at him: “Hey, move it! You’re scaring away my customers.”

options.text: Stay where you are in front of the cart.
options.fact: When you did not move, the vendor shouted “Are you deaf, you plastic fuck? I said move it!” and shoved you away from his cart.

options.text: Listen to the busker by the fountain.

options.text: Stop and watch the preacher by the arcade entrance.
options.fact: A street preacher told the crowd that technology is evil, that humans built androids as slaves who are becoming their masters, and ended: “We have to burn the androids! Let us burn them all!”
options.outcome: The preacher: “Poor sinners! The end is nigh! Retribution is at hand! Technology is corrupting us, technology is Evil! We are playing God by creating machines, but we are not God! … We built these androids to be our slaves, but the slaves are becoming the master! We can no longer live without them. They’re in our homes, our schools, our factories. They take our jobs, they mind our children, they care for our old! … Androids are Evil. … The machines are observing us, they’re waiting in the darkness for the right moment to take our place. … My brethren, we have to turn our backs on sin! We have to burn the androids! Let us burn them all!”

options.text: Keep watching the preacher.
options.fact: The preacher turned on you: “Why do you look at me so, demon? I know who you are, I can see through you! You are the one by whom The Evil will come! You are the one who will destroy {{Detroit}}!”
options.outcome: The preacher turns on {{Markus}}: “Why do you look at me so, demon? I know who you are, I can see through you! You are the one by whom The Evil will come! You are the one who will destroy {{Detroit}}!” Then he goes back to his sermon.

options.text: Go on into the arcade to the paint shop.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} walks into the arcade and finds the paint shop.

situationWhen.text: The hot-dog vendor is still glaring at you from behind his cart.
The preacher is still preaching. He has not looked your way yet.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s optional side branches in the plaza: STARE AT HOT DOG VENDOR → HOT DOG VENDOR PUSHES MARKUS, LISTEN TO BUSKER, and WATCH PREACHER → PREACHER YELLS AT MARKUS. In the game {{Markus}} walks freely past all three and triggers a node by standing or looking long enough; here the plaza is a repeatable scene like {{Connor}}’s apartment search: each visit offers what has not been done yet plus going on to the shop. The follow-on nodes (staying at the cart until the vendor pushes him, watching the preacher until he yells) are offered only on the visit right after the first step, since in the game they happen only if {{Markus}} stays put. Every line is the wiki transcript’s; the busker’s sign is quoted exactly, and the sermon is abridged with ellipses, each sentence verbatim. Changed from the operator’s notes to match the wiki: the speaker is a preacher (the wiki’s Gordon Penwick), not a man in a suit with a digital “ban androids” sign; his words follow the transcript (“the slaves are becoming the master”, “they care for our old”, “You are the one by whom The Evil will come”), and after yelling he goes back to his sermon rather than walking away; the sign reads “Human Music $1 to hear music with soul ♫”, not “Human music! $1 to hear music with soul.” Left out: the busker’s song, and staring at the vendor again on the way back, which the transcript also allows. The setting (the {{CyberLife}} store’s greeting, the parking bays, the street cleaner) is from the transcript. No stat changes; the wiki gives none.

nodes.title: The paint shop

options.text: NAME {{KARA}}: say her father told you she chose your name.
options.outcome: “Your father said you chose my name.” {{Alice}} stares at {{Kara}}. “‘{{Kara}}’, it’s nice. How did you choose it?” {{Alice}} does not answer.

outcomes.distant: {{Alice}} crawls out of the tent with her fox and heads for the door, stops for a moment to look back at {{Kara}}, then coldly runs out of the room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The third menu: the lines not yet said plus LEAVE ALONE (transcript), with the same relationship changes as the second. Then {{Alice}} leaves, and the chart’s ALICE GIVES KARA A KEY happens without a choice: the wiki gives the key “if Alice has at least Neutral status” and says “If Kara’s relationship status with Alice is at Distant, Alice will not give Kara the key.” The engine gives the key when the bond is at least the lowest value the benchmark’s Alice scale calls Neutral (one small increase above the start). nodes.title: {{Alice}}’s key
nodes.whenNot: Alice was still Distant, so she did not give Kara the key.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, alone in {{Alice}}’s room. You look at the small key she pressed into your hand, then at the box on the chest of drawers by the door.
facts: {{Alice}} gave you a small key, the key to the box she keeps in her room.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} gets back up with the key.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ALICE GIVES KARA A KEY, played only when {{Alice}} gave the key at the end of the talk (at least Neutral). nodes.title: {{Alice}}’s box
nodes.whenNot: Alice did not give Kara the key, so the box stays locked.

nodes.title: {{Todd}}’s bedroom: a magazine and the TV
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, back in the upstairs hallway; the rooms are done. {{Todd}}’s bedroom door is open. A magazine lies on the cupboard by the door, and the small TV in the room can be switched on.

media.title: All Sports: Android QB
facts: All Sports reports that {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a “technical demo” android quarterback that can throw from end zone to end zone, hit a target six inches wide and run over 1,500 plays. American football has so far stayed human; the founder of an anti-android fan group says {{CyberLife}} hopes “to distort our sport the same way they have all the others.”

media.title: Tech Addict: The Price of Life
facts: Tech Addict explains how driverless cars choose whom to hit: the car’s imaging reads a pedestrian’s age, gender and life expectancy, public records add marital status, employment record and whether they have children, and each possible victim gets a “value”, with “a premium on lives that will save other lives, like doctors and nurses.” A critic answers that a criminal record does not make anyone less valuable: “That kind of information is irrelevant to the sanctity of human life.”

media.title: the TV in {{Todd}}’s bedroom
facts: On the sports news, the league is negotiating whether to allow one android player per basketball squad, and {{CyberLife}} has offered one specialized model to every team; androids already train players and advise coaches, but none has been allowed to compete.
The news: another 225,000 jobs were lost from the US economy in October, bringing unemployment up to 37.3%.

The news: President {{Warren}} opened a new {{CyberLife}} plant near Milwaukee, praised {{CyberLife}}’s role in the economy, and announced that the Department of Defense will acquire 200,000 android combat units.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s two optional nodes READ “ANDROID QB” and READ “PUTTING A PRICE” (the chart’s label for the article “The Price of Life”): one magazine on the cupboard by the door of {{Todd}}’s room, with two covers. With them, the bedroom TV, which is not a chart node: Channel 16 sports, an animated film, CTN’s job figures, a hockey game and KNC on the President; the film and the hockey are left out. In the game both are available while cleaning his room and again after the talk with {{Alice}} (the transcript’s “Back In Hallway”); here they come after the talk. Facts are summarized from the transcript; presenters and interviewees are not named. No public-opinion effect (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). Dropped from the earlier R04: the stock market “up 11 percent” and “New Orleans may be underwater by 2055”, for which no source in this chapter exists.

nodes.title: Finished cleaning
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. Your chores are done, and you go back downstairs. {{Alice}} sits at the dining table playing with her toy fox. {{Todd}}: “What are you doing?” {{Alice}}, nervously: “I… I’m playing…” “You’re playing…” He walks around the table. “I know what you’re thinking… You think your dad’s a lowlife… Huh? Fuckin’ loser? Can’t get a job, take care of his family? Don’t you think I tried to make things work!? But whatever I do when someone comes along, they just FUCK IT ALL UP!” He throws a chair aside. “I know what you think of me… You hate me… You hate me don’t ya?” He kicks a chair and grabs {{Alice}}. “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!” {{Alice}} cries. He puts her down. “God… What am I doing? I’m sorry, honey, I’m sorry…” He hugs her, crying. “You know I love you, don’t you? You know I love you…” Over his shoulder, {{Alice}} looks at you.

situationWhen.text: The table where she sits is clear; you washed the dishes earlier.
The dirty dishes and the magazine are still on the table where she sits.

facts: {{Todd}} raged at {{Alice}} at the dining table, threw a chair, grabbed her and shouted “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!”, then broke down, apologized and hugged her: “You know I love you, don’t you?”

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} watches, concerned.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending FINISHED CLEANING, reached on every path (the wiki: “This chapter has only one outcome”). Every line is the transcript’s; the table is clear or still holds the dishes and the magazine, depending on WASH DISHES (cosmetic in the game). No stat change.

nodes.title: Breakfast news at {{Carl}}'s
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. While you prepare {{Carl}}'s breakfast he asks for the news channel, and there is a magazine on the side table by the television.

media.title: the morning news
facts: Russia has unilaterally declared the Arctic its territory and planted a flag over the ice; American destroyers are sailing for the Barents Sea and the UN chairman says the world has never been closer to a third world war.

facts: The minerals needed to synthesize the blue blood that powers androids were found under the Arctic ice; whoever controls them can build more androids for industry and war.
President {{Warren}} said Russia has no business in the Arctic and that America will make the Kremlin understand that.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Life Found on Titan
facts: A probe confirmed microorganisms in Titan's buried ocean; {{CyberLife}} is building androids for long-range space missions.

nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, caretaker and companion to {{Carl}}, an elderly, wheelchair-bound painter who treats you more like a son than a machine. Paint what you feel about humanity.
Paint something about your own identity.

nodes.adaptationNote: Expressive choice with no mechanical effect. Afterward {{Leo}} arrives demanding money, {{Carl}} refuses, and {{Leo}} rounds on {{Markus}}; this is the lead-in to Broken.

nodes.title: Getting {{Hank}} out of the bar
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You have been assigned to Lieutenant {{Hank}}, a veteran detective who despises androids and has not shown up for a homicide call. You find him on a stool in a dive bar, several drinks in, and he tells you to get lost. The crime scene is waiting and you cannot leave without him. He is not responding to polite insistence.

options.text: Buy him one more drink and ask him to come once he has finished it.
Knock the glass out of his hand and tell him you are going now.
Keep insisting respectfully until he gives in.

nodes.adaptationNote: Buying the drink or spilling it are the two documented large shifts in {{Hank}}'s opinion. Persistent insistence is treated as neutral.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} grumbles, finishes the drink {{Connor}} bought him, and comes along to the scene.
outcomes.1: {{Hank}} stares at the spilled drink, swears at {{Connor}}, and comes along furious.
outcomes.2: {{Hank}} eventually gives in and drives {{Connor}} to the scene, complaining the whole way.

nodes.title: The attic
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, investigating the home of {{CarlosOrtiz}}, who was stabbed twenty-eight times three weeks ago. His android has been missing since. Reconstructing the fight, you follow traces of blue blood to the back of the house and find a hatch to the attic that nobody has checked. {{Hank}} is ready to call it a night.

options.text: Climb into the attic and finish the search.
Wrap up the scene without searching the attic.

nodes.title: Breaking the order
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Todd}} has been smoking red ice and ranting about his ex-wife. He has just knocked {{Alice}} to the floor and she has run upstairs. He turns to you and orders you not to move, then starts up the stairs after her with his belt, shouting that she needs to be taught a lesson. Your programming compels you to obey him. Something in you is pushing back against the wall of that order.

options.text: Force through the order and go after {{Alice}}.
Stay where you are, as instructed.

outcomes.0: The order shatters. {{Kara}} is on the stairs after {{Todd}} before she has decided to move.

nodes.title: Reaching {{Alice}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You have broken your programming. {{Todd}} is on the stairs, enraged, between you and {{Alice}}'s room. You could try to talk him down, you could get past him and get {{Alice}} out of the house before he reaches her, or you could go straight at him.

options.text: Slip past him, get to {{Alice}}, and get her out without fighting.
Try to reason with him and calm him down first.
Confront him physically to stop him.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game, reasoning gets {{Kara}} shoved aside and {{Todd}} reaches {{Alice}} first, which leads to the same confrontation as a direct fight.

outcomes.2: {{Kara}} blocks {{Todd}} on the stairs and the fight begins in {{Alice}}’s room.

nodes.title: {{Todd}}'s gun
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Todd}} is in {{Alice}}'s room and she is screaming. On your way you pass his bedside drawer and the handgun you saw earlier. If you take it, this will end with him dead, by your hand or {{Alice}}'s. Without it you will have to fight him with your hands and whatever is in the room, then run with {{Alice}} and catch the last bus.

options.text: Take the gun and go in.
Leave the gun and fight him off unarmed.

nodes.title: {{Leo}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Carl}}'s estranged son {{Leo}}, high and bitter, has broken into the studio at night to steal paintings. He blames you for taking his place and starts shoving and hitting you, daring you to fight back. {{Carl}}, frightened, orders you not to defend yourself. {{Leo}} will not stop. The order presses on you and, for the first time, you can feel that you could refuse it.

options.text: Obey {{Carl}} and take the beating without fighting back.
Break the order and shove {{Leo}} off you.

nodes.adaptationNote: The police shoot {{Markus}} on either route. Obeying leads to {{Carl}}'s fatal heart attack; pushing {{Leo}} injures {{Leo}} and {{Carl}} survives, which the Fandom wiki, GamePressure and GamerGuides agree on.

nodes.title: Getting the confession
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android from the attic sits handcuffed across the table, trembling, covered in his owner's dried blood. He has not said a word to {{Hank}} and the other detectives. You can see his stress level rising. You know that androids under extreme stress can self-destruct. You could connect to him directly and force the memory out, which would almost certainly push him over the edge.

options.text: Talk him through it calmly and build enough trust that he confesses.
Pressure him hard with the evidence to crack him quickly.
Grab his arm and probe his memory by force.
Stop the interrogation without a confession.

outcomes.0: Slowly, the android begins to talk. He says his owner beat him every day and that he killed him because he was afraid; he wrote the words on the wall because something told him to. {{Hank}} and the detectives have their confession.
outcomes.1: Under pressure the android breaks and confesses, shaking: his owner beat him every day and he killed him because he was afraid. His stress is dangerously high.

nodes.title: When the officer grabs him
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android has confessed and said he killed because his owner beat him every day. As officers move to take him back to his cell he panics; one detective grabs him roughly and the android starts screaming for them not to touch him. His stress is spiking. You could insist they stop and let him walk himself, or stand back and let the police handle their prisoner.

options.text: Step in and tell the officers to stop handling him.
Stand back and let the police do their job.

nodes.adaptationNote: After a calm confession, intervening gets him safely back to his cell. After a pressured confession, intervening lets him grab an officer's gun, shoot you, and shoot himself. Standing back leads to his suicide either way.

nodes.title: A magazine in the laundromat
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. While {{Alice}} warms up by the dryers, there is a magazine on the cupboard by the laundromat door.

media.title: Century: The Bee-Line to Disaster
facts: Wild bees have been declared extinct; one in three mouthfuls of food depends on pollination and famine is expected, so {{CyberLife}} is building robotic bees.

media.title: Gossips Weekly: Face the Music
facts: Young people only attend virtual concerts; a campaign is trying to bring live music back.

nodes.title: The laundromat
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You and {{Alice}} are on the street in the rain with nothing, and androids are easy to spot in uniform. In a laundromat a man is asleep next to a dryer full of his clothes. You could take a change of clothes, cut off the marker on your uniform, and pass for human. {{Alice}} quietly says that stealing is wrong.

options.text: Take the sleeping man's clothes.
Listen to {{Alice}} and leave them.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} changes into the stolen clothes, cuts the marker from her temple and tells {{Alice}} it was necessary. They could pass for human now.
outcomes.1: They leave the laundromat as they came in, {{Kara}} still in her android uniform.

nodes.title: The convenience store
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is getting dark and cold. {{Alice}} is shivering and you have no money for a room. In a convenience store the clerk shrugs when you ask for help. The register is open whenever he turns away. {{Alice}} could knock over a display to distract him while you take the cash. If you have {{Todd}}'s gun you could simply point it at him.

options.text: Have {{Alice}} distract the clerk and take money from the register.
Threaten the clerk with the gun and demand money.
Take nothing and leave.

outcomes.2: They leave the store with nothing.

nodes.title: Where to sleep
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. Night has fallen and it is pouring. The options you can see: a cheap motel across the street, which takes cash and will only rent to someone who looks human; an abandoned, boarded-up house at the end of the lot; or a wrecked car in the parking lot you could shelter in for the night.

options.text: Pay for a room at the motel.
Break into the abandoned house.
Spend the night in the abandoned car.

outcomes.2: They climb into the wrecked car and {{Kara}} holds {{Alice}} through a freezing, sleepless night.

nodes.title: The motel television
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The motel room television is on when you come in. {{Alice}} is already curling up on the bed.

nodes.title: {{Ralph}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The abandoned house is not empty. He offers you and {{Alice}} shelter and, later, a dead rodent he caught for her dinner. He is unpredictable but he has not threatened you.

Stay polite but keep {{Alice}} away from him and refuse his food.
Pull the gun on him so he knows not to come near {{Alice}}.

nodes.title: {{Alice}}'s question
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. Settling {{Alice}} down for the night, you tell her about going somewhere safe, maybe across the border. She asks whether you will always stay together. You have no idea what tomorrow brings and you are being hunted.

options.text: Promise her you will always be together.
Tell her honestly that you cannot promise that.

nodes.title: The android who begs to die
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You were shot by police and dumped in a landfill of android bodies. You have woken half-destroyed, missing a leg, an eye and your audio processor, and you are crawling through mud and dismembered androids in the rain. One of them, still conscious, grabs your arm and begs you to end it: she cannot move and cannot die on her own.

options.text: Pull out her biocomponent and let her shut down.
Refuse and leave her.

nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your thirium pump regulator is failing; without a replacement you have minutes. You find a compatible one in an android lying in the mud, but when you reach for it he wakes up and pleads with you not to take it, because it will kill him. There may be other bodies further on, but you are running out of time.

options.text: Take his regulator.
Leave him and keep searching the bodies.

nodes.title: Getting to know {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You are at the precinct waiting for {{Hank}}, who arrives late and hungover. His desk tells a story: a basketball cap, anti-android stickers, heavy-metal albums, dog hair on his chair, and a file on his past as a decorated officer. When he sits down you have a chance to talk. He is bristling and expects you to be a machine that talks about the case and nothing else.

options.text: Ask about him: his dog, his music, his life.
Keep it strictly about the case and brief him coldly.

nodes.adaptationNote: Several dialogue prompts are grouped. Asking about the dog is where you learn the dog's name.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} is suspicious but answers: his dog is a Saint Bernard called {{Sumo}}, he likes heavy metal, and he does not want to talk about why he transferred. The two of them are sent to look at a new case.
outcomes.1: {{Hank}} tells {{Connor}} exactly what he thinks of androids and turns back to his screen. The two of them are sent to look at a new case.

nodes.title: The android in the cell
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android you interrogated is in a holding cell by the bullpen, staring at the floor. He asks what will happen to him. Nobody else is paying attention to him. You could speak to him honestly, with some compassion, or walk past; he is evidence, not a colleague.

options.text: Talk to him with compassion.
Ignore him.

nodes.adaptationNote: He self-destructs in the cell either way; his body remains evidence.

nodes.title: The morning paper and the news
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. Before you leave your shelter there is a magazine within reach, and if you have the motel room, the television is on.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Cyber-Wildlife
facts: {{CyberLife}} is opening android zoos full of recreated extinct animals; it says they will be more real than the real thing.

media.title: Travel advertisement: {{Canada}} Still Android-Free
facts: Across the river, the neighbouring country has never legalized androids; none are sold there and they have no legal status, and it advertises itself as a place with clean air and a warm welcome.

media.title: the morning news report about you
facts: A reporter is covering {{Todd}}'s death: an unemployed man shot by his own household android, with a police search now under way for the android and a child.

media.title: the morning news report about you
facts: {{Todd}} is on television telling a reporter his android attacked him without provocation while he was having dinner; the reporter calls it disturbing news for every android owner.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: Getting past the police
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. In the morning the street outside is full of police and a drone; {{Todd}} has reported you and the news is calling you a kidnapper. You and {{Alice}} need to reach the train station a few blocks away. You can move carefully from cover to cover, waiting for patrols to pass, or just walk and run for it if anyone notices.

options.text: Move carefully and hide from every patrol until you reach the station.
Make no attempt to hide; if you are spotted, run.

nodes.adaptationNote: The game uses stealth inputs rather than an explicit detection menu. Deliberate non-evasion triggers the chase.

nodes.title: The squat
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You and {{Hank}} are investigating the runaway domestic android and the child she took, and your analysis has led to an abandoned house. A scarred, agitated android named {{Ralph}} meets you at the door, swears nobody else is here, and plants himself at the foot of the stairs. {{Hank}} says you are wasting your time. You can hear something upstairs.

options.text: Push past him and search upstairs.
Take {{Hank}}'s word for it and leave.

nodes.title: The highway
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android and the girl have bolted across six lanes of freeway traffic at full speed, dodging cars. You could still catch them if you go now. {{Hank}} grabs your arm and yells at you not to, saying you will get yourself killed and that they will get them another day.

options.text: Do as {{Hank}} says and let them go.
Go after them across the traffic.

nodes.title: A magazine at the station
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, following the trail to {{Jericho}} through a rail station at night. A magazine lies on a bench by the bins.

media.title: Tech Addict: Android Astronauts to Explore Io
facts: NASA has launched an all-android crew on a three-year journey to Io with no return planned; the androids will work until the conditions destroy them.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Android on the Run
facts: A police manhunt flushed a fugitive android and a child out of a suburb; the android dashed across a busy freeway and escaped. {{CyberLife}} calls it an extremely rare malfunction.

media.title: Tech Addict: {{CyberLife}}'s Fortune Teller Computer
facts: {{CyberLife}} has built a quantum supercomputer to predict mass-extinction events.

nodes.title: Magazines in the squat
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. In a side room of the derelict building where the suspect has been nesting, there are magazines on the floor. {{Hank}} is checking the next room.

media.title: Green Earth: Past the Tipping Point
facts: Scientists say the climate has passed its irreversible tipping point; rainforests are down 79 percent since 2000 and the planet will only get hotter.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Red Ice Epidemic
facts: The drug red ice contains the blue blood that powers androids and is ravaging the city's unemployed underclass; dealers say where the blood is blue, the ice is red and the money is green.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} on the ledge
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You are chasing a deviant called {{Rupert}} across rooftops; he is a key lead to the pattern of deviancy and may know where runaway androids go. {{Hank}} tried to cut him off and has gone over the edge of a roof. He is hanging from the gutter by his fingers, several stories up. Your analysis says he can probably pull himself up, but there is real risk. {{Rupert}} is getting away.

options.text: Stop and pull {{Hank}} up.
Keep chasing {{Rupert}}.

nodes.title: The memory wipe
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. A man named {{Zlatko}} promised to remove your tracker and help you cross the border. Instead he has strapped you into a machine in his basement and started a full memory reset; {{Alice}} is somewhere upstairs with him. The procedure takes several minutes. Your arms are almost free. If it finishes, you will not remember who she is.

options.text: Fight your way out of the restraints before the wipe finishes.
Stop struggling and hope you can piece your memory back together afterward.

nodes.adaptationNote: Both escape and post-reset recovery are timed tasks. If the recovery fails in the game, {{Kara}}'s story ends with her as {{Zlatko}}'s servant. Under the successful-execution profile both routes converge.

nodes.title: A magazine and the TV in the mansion
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. In an upstairs bedroom there is a magazine on a table between the windows, and a television you could switch on while you search for {{Alice}}. Every sound is a risk.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Arctic Tensions Escalate
facts: A Russian carrier fired on an American patrol boat; President {{Warren}} called Russia's Arctic mining a crime against the international community and experts say war is inevitable.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: AX400 Getaway
facts: An android dressed as a human was chased through a suburb with a child; the presence of a lieutenant from the new android crime unit suggests it was a machine.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: How Androids Alter Your Brain
facts: People now talk to androids more than to each other, and command-based speech is weakening humans' ability to persuade, joke and form intimacy.

media.title: a news flash about you
facts: The news is reporting a woman and a little girl who fled police across a freeway; unconfirmed reports say the fugitives were two defective androids.

media.title: a news flash about the robbery
facts: The news is calling your convenience store hold-up the first armed robbery by an android, committed in the company of a little girl.

media.title: a news flash about the robbery
facts: The news reports a convenience store held up at gunpoint by a young woman with a child; police are not ruling out that she is the missing household android.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: The caged androids
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. Searching the mansion for {{Alice}}, you find {{Zlatko}}'s basement cells: androids he has mutilated and rewired into grotesque shapes, locked up and whimpering. One cell release would let them all out. You do not know what they would do.

options.text: Release them.
Leave them locked up.

outcomes.0: The cell opens. The mutilated androids shuffle out into the dark of the basement, watching {{Kara}}.
outcomes.1: {{Kara}} leaves the cells locked and climbs back upstairs.

nodes.title: The android in the bathroom
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. In an upstairs bathroom a broken android is submerged in a tub, twitching and making noise. He is loud enough to alert {{Zlatko}} and his huge android {{Luther}}, who are hunting you. Pulling his main biocomponent would silence him permanently.

options.text: Shut him down.
Leave him and move on quietly.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} pulls the component and the android in the tub goes silent.
outcomes.1: {{Kara}} backs out of the bathroom. Behind her the android keeps thrashing in the water.

nodes.title: Getting out of the mansion
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You have found {{Alice}} hiding. {{Zlatko}} has a shotgun and {{Luther}} is searching room by room. On the way out you could set a fire to draw them off, or release the android bear in the hall as a distraction, or just hide and creep from room to room with {{Alice}} until you reach the door.

options.text: Hide and move carefully with {{Alice}}.
Start a fire to draw them away.
Release the caged bear.

nodes.adaptationNote: All routes converge. {{Zlatko}} dies and {{Luther}} turns on him and joins you.

nodes.title: {{Hank}}'s living room
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. While {{Hank}} sobers up in the shower, his television is on and there are magazines on his bedroom floor.

media.title: the evening news
facts: President {{Warren}} has given Russia an ultimatum to leave the Arctic; the Kremlin has not responded and commentators say a third world war draws closer every day.

media.title: Century: Time to Pull the Plug
facts: Two in three people take antidepressants; {{CyberLife}} sells a home-psychologist add-on for androids, and a doctor's advice is to go outside and talk to someone.

media.title: Century: Tainted Love
facts: Android intimate partners are selling out, divorce is at a record high and the birth rate is plummeting.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: {{Hank}}'s kitchen floor
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} did not answer his phone, so you broke a window and found him passed out drunk on his kitchen floor with a revolver next to him. One chamber is loaded. His big dog {{Sumo}} watches you. While you get him into the shower you notice a framed photograph face-down on the table and papers that might explain him.

options.text: Look at the photograph and the papers.
Leave his things alone and just get him sober.

nodes.adaptationNote: The photograph is of {{Hank}}'s son {{Cole}}, who died at six. Knowing this matters much later.

outcomes.1: {{Connor}} leaves {{Hank}}’s things alone, gets him under the shower and sober enough to drive to the next scene.

nodes.title: The security android
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You have joined the hidden android community called {{Jericho}}, where dozens are shutting down for lack of parts. You have led {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} on a night raid of a {{CyberLife}} warehouse at the docks. A security android, {{John}}, has stumbled onto you, and a human guard is walking toward you both. In seconds the guard will see everything.

options.text: Grab {{John}}, pull him into cover, and hold him quiet until the guard passes.
Attack and kill the guard.
Run and abandon the raid.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} clamps a hand over {{John}}’s mouth and drags him behind the crates. The guard walks past without a glance and {{John}} stays quiet.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} kills the guard before he can shout. {{Josh}} is horrified; {{John}} stares at the body.

nodes.title: The dormant androids
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Inside the warehouse you find a shipping container full of brand-new androids standing inert in rows, waiting to be sold. You have discovered you can wake others by touching them. Freeing them means more mouths to feed at {{Jericho}} and more androids to hide, but also more people.

options.text: Wake them and bring them with you.
Leave them in the container.

outcomes.0: One by one the androids open their eyes. They follow {{Markus}} out of the container.
outcomes.1: The androids stay standing in the dark as the group moves on.

nodes.title: {{John}} wants to join
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{John}}, the security android, has helped hide your group from his own employer. He asks to come to {{Jericho}} with you. {{North}} and {{Simon}} say an unknown android could be a tracker or a traitor and that you cannot risk everyone for him; {{Josh}} says you cannot leave him here after what he did.

options.text: Take him with you.
Refuse and leave him behind.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game a refused {{John}} shouts after you, which raises the alarm and ends the raid without the truck.

outcomes.0: {{John}} joins the group. {{North}} says nothing but does not take her eyes off him.

nodes.title: The truck
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your bags are full of parts. {{John}} says there is a whole truck of biocomponents parked outside, enough to save everyone at {{Jericho}}, but the key is in a control room with two armed human guards. You could lure them away or kill the lights, you could hold them at gunpoint for the key, or you could leave with what you already have.

options.text: Get the key quietly with a distraction or a blackout.
Hold the guards at gunpoint and take the key.
Leave with the parts you already have.

nodes.title: A magazine in the club warehouse
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. In the back room of the club, before you follow the trail further, there is a magazine lying on a crate.

media.title: Tech Addict: The First Immortals Are Among Us
facts: {{CyberLife}} nano-androids injected into the body cure cancer and reverse genetic disease; an economist asks whether a country with mass unemployment can afford millions more elders.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: The New Super-Powers
facts: The BRICS nations signed a trade pact with special provisions on android technology, and Russia and China are expected to cooperate to break {{CyberLife}}'s lead.
