nodes.title: The two {{Tracis}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. A man was strangled in a sex club by a rented android; you tracked the android and her lover through the club, two women who were trying to run away together. In the warehouse they attacked you and {{Hank}} to escape; you have beaten one to the ground and have a gun on her while the other watches. They are not fighting any more. They say they only wanted to be together, away from men who used them. {{Hank}} has not told you what to do.

options.text: Lower the gun and let them go.
Shoot them.

nodes.title: The car radio and a magazine in the tavern
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. On the drive to the abandoned park the radio can play the news, and inside the derelict tavern there is a magazine on the barrels where you set down the flashlight.

media.title: the radio news
facts: An American submarine has vanished in Arctic waters; President {{Warren}} says Russian aggression has reached a new level and commentators call it a war waiting to start.

media.title: the radio news about the mansion fire
facts: Local news reports a house fire on the outskirts with an unidentified body and dozens of androids found in the ruins.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: USS Iowa Missing
facts: The missing submarine was last seen in the Arctic; the Kremlin denies involvement and says an American warship had no business there.

media.title: Gossips Weekly: All-Android Band Tipped for Music Prize
facts: An all-android boy band is tipped for a top music award; less than 5 percent of the music market is now made by humans.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: Strangers in the dark
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} are sheltering in a derelict amusement park at night. Figures step out of the dark around your fire, identical androids in park uniforms, several of them, approaching silently. {{Luther}} has a gun in his bag. There is a burning stick at your feet.

options.text: Put yourself in front of {{Alice}} and ask them what they want.
Grab a burning stick and warn them off.
Grab the gun from {{Luther}}'s bag and fire a warning shot.

nodes.adaptationNote: The androids are harmless entertainers who want to show {{Alice}} the carousel. All responses converge.

outcomes.0: The androids stop. They are entertainers from the park, all the same model, and they only wanted to show {{Alice}} the carousel. They light it up for her and she laughs for the first time in days.
outcomes.1: The androids raise their hands. They are entertainers from the park, all the same model, and they only wanted to show {{Alice}} the carousel. They light it up for her and she laughs for the first time in days.
outcomes.2: The shot echoes and the androids freeze with their hands up. They are harmless entertainers from the park who only wanted to show {{Alice}} the carousel. Once {{Kara}} lowers the gun they light it up for her.

nodes.title: A magazine on the park bench
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} has walked ahead to the riverside bench. A magazine lies on the red bench by the path.

media.title: Century: The Mysterious Mister {{Kamski}}
facts: {{Kamski}} founded {{CyberLife}} in 2018 in a cheap part of the city, broke through with blue blood and biocomponents, was named Man of the Century in 2028, then left the company after clashing with shareholders and now lives in a waterside villa exclusively with androids.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Markets Predict War
facts: Stock markets are pricing in an Arctic war; military stocks are booming and investors favour {{CyberLife}} for its defence contracts.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: What are you?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. After the club, {{Hank}} sits on a bench by the river at night, drinking, and asks you things no one has asked you: whether you are afraid to die, whether you have ever thought about what it is like, why you let those two go if you are just a machine. He pulls out his gun and points it at your head, saying he wants to know what happens when he pulls the trigger. How you answer him will decide what he thinks you are.

options.text: Answer him honestly, admitting doubt and something like fear.
Insist that you are a machine, that you feel nothing, and that his questions are irrelevant.

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Hank}} shoots {{Connor}} only if his relationship is Hostile at this point, regardless of the answer.

nodes.title: Alone in {{Ferndale}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. It is 9:24 in the morning on November 7th, and you are walking alone through {{Ferndale}}. On the street a man berates an android: “You klutz! Pick them up! And make it snappy!” Back in {{Jericho}}, you tell {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}}: “We can’t stay silent anymore. It’s time humans heard what we have to say.” {{Simon}}: “You know they’ll never listen to us…” {{Josh}}: “And revealing ourselves will put us in danger.” You: “If we want freedom, we need to have the courage to ask for it. That’s the only way.” {{North}}: “What do you wanna do?” You: “{{Channel16}} broadcasts from the {{Stratford}} Tower. The control room is on the top floor. That’s where we need to go. We’ll plan the operation down to the smallest detail. We can’t leave anything to chance.”
facts: In {{Ferndale}} you saw a man berate an android: “You klutz! Pick them up! And make it snappy!”
Your plan: take the {{Channel16}} control room on the top floor of the {{Stratford}} Tower and broadcast a message from the androids to the humans.

outcomes.0: The next afternoon, {{Markus}} walks into the {{Stratford}} Tower.

nodes.adaptationNote: The prologue’s four chart nodes, ALONE IN {{FERNDALE}} (checkpoint), WITNESS ANDROID DISCRIMINATION, BACK IN {{JERICHO}} and {{MARKUS}} EXPLAINS HIS PLAN, as one narrated event. Every line is the template’s; the time and date are the transcript header’s. The template gives only the man’s words, so the scene around them is not described. The Tech Addict article visible in the cutscene is unreadable and not a collectible, so it is left out. No stat change.

nodes.title: The lobby
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, walking into the lobby of the {{Stratford}} Tower at 1:30 in the afternoon on November 8th. The others are waiting for you to open the way. Security gates bar the way to the elevators. Behind the front desk sit an android receptionist and, at the left side of the desk, her human supervisor. Nearby, a man on the phone is buying stock: “Heuristics Digital is selling at 2.50… You got me. I’ll take 2000.” You need to get past security.

options.text: Talk to the android receptionist behind the front desk.
Leave the receptionist for now and look over the supervisor and her desk.

outcomes.0: The receptionist: “Hello, sir. What can I do for you?” {{Markus}}: “I’m okay, thanks.” With her supervisor sitting beside her, there is nothing more to say. He turns his attention to the supervisor.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} turns his attention to the supervisor.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint {{STRATFORD}} TOWER and the phase [FIND A WAY TO PASS SECURITY]. TALK TO ANDROID RECEPTIONIST is an optional grey node with no outgoing edge: with her supervisor beside her the receptionist only offers help and {{Markus}} declines (the template’s lines; wiki note). It is not a button prompt in the game, so the options carry no label. Either way the desk analysis follows. The man on the phone is the template’s “Man on the phone”, quoted in part. No stat change.

nodes.title: Analyze supervisor’s desk
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You analyze the supervisor at the front desk and everything on and around her: her smart watch, the photo of her daughter, her name plate, her parking badge and her home address.
facts: Supervisor’s desk, SMART WATCH: MODEL T215. Phone number: 555 847 33.
Supervisor’s desk, {{WILSON}}, {{EMILY}}: Supervisor’s Daughter. Child registered at: {{SaintRose}} school.
Supervisor’s desk, {{WILSON}}, {{ELIZABETH}}: Born: 03/25/1999. Desk manager.
Supervisor’s desk, PARKING BADGE: Car registration - API 1704. Floor -3 - Spot A21.
Supervisor’s desk, HOME ADDRESS: 4685 {{MichiganStreet}}, {{Detroit}}. Fire safety rating: poor.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has her phone number, and three reasons she might leave her desk.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart node ANALYZE SUPERVISOR’S DESK and the template’s observation group, as a narrated event: the five clues, with the game’s titles and sublines, become facts. In the game each clue is a separate look; here {{Markus}} analyzes all of them, as PowerPyx advises (“Analyze all clues on and around her. This will give you 3 options”), so all three phone ruses are open on every path. The objects named in the situation are inferred from the clue titles. No stat change.

nodes.title: Call supervisor
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You call the supervisor’s number from across the lobby. She answers: “{{Elizabeth}} {{Wilson}} speaking?” You need a reason that will make her leave her desk.

options.text: PARKING: pose as the parking attendant and tell her someone has backed into her car.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Good morning, Ms. {{Wilson}}. Sorry to bother you, this is Mike from the car park. There’s a problem with your car.” Supervisor: “Problem? What kind of problem?” {{Markus}}: “Somebody’s backed into it. You better come take a look.” Supervisor: “Are you serious? Oh, God, alright… Fine, I’ll be right down.” She leaves the desk.

options.text: SCHOOL: pose as her daughter’s school and tell her {{Emily}} has a fever.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “This is {{SaintRose}} school, ma’am. Your daughter {{Emily}} has a fever. It’s nothing serious but I think you’d better come and pick her up.” Supervisor: “Oh, no! Alright… I’ll… I’ll be right there.” She leaves the desk.

options.text: FIRE DEPARTMENT: pose as a fireman and tell her there has been a fire in her building.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Yeah, hello? This is the {{Detroit}} fire department. Listen, do you live at 4685 {{MichiganStreet}}?” Supervisor: “Yes…” {{Markus}}: “Er... yes, ma’am. There’s been a fire in your building. You think you can come down here?” Supervisor: “Oh… Oh, God… Okay, I’ll be right there.” She leaves the desk.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CALL SUPERVISOR and the template’s PROMPT 1, with its three buttons in the template’s order (the chart lists them as POSE AS FIREMAN, POSE AS TEACHER and POSE AS PARKING ATTENDANT). Each is bracketed in the template, the site’s mark for an option that needs an unlock; each requires the desk clue it uses. Every path leads to SUPERVISOR LEAVES (PowerPyx: “Regardless of your choice she leaves”). The lines are the template’s. No stat change (the wiki: “This has no mechanical effect whatsoever”).

nodes.title: The unsupervised receptionist
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. With the supervisor gone, you go back to the android receptionist. You: “I have an appointment with Mr. {{Peterson}}.” Receptionist: “Do you have any ID?” You: “Yeah. Yes, of course.” You touch her hand and wake her: “I need your help.” Receptionist: “I’ve just checked your ID. The elevators are after the security gate.” You: “Thanks.” You pass security and take the elevator up to the forty-seventh floor.
facts: You woke the android receptionist in the {{Stratford}} Tower lobby; she let you through security to the elevators.

outcomes.0: The elevator doors open on the forty-seventh floor.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO UNSUPERVISED ANDROID RECEPTIONIST, CONVERT RECEPTIONIST, PASS SECURITY and TAKE ELEVATOR, all unmissable (PowerPyx), as one narrated event with the template’s lines. That {{Markus}} wakes her by touch is how conversion works elsewhere in the game; the template gives only “I need your help.” No stat change.

nodes.title: At floor 47
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, stepping out of the elevator on the forty-seventh floor, where {{Channel16}}’s staff work. Two women complain about their jobs: “God, I am so tired of this place!” “I hear {{KNC}} is hiring.” “I guess the pay would be better…” “Couldn’t be any worse.” “Max said they’re finally sending androids into space.” “People can’t get jobs, and we’re sending rockets into space! I mean, y’know, what do they even expect to find up there?” A woman tells a colleague he looks beat; he says he could really use a coffee. On a couch, a man asks a woman whether she would like to do something sometime; she lets him down gently, and he says he is going to check out the {{CyberLife}} zoo: “If only I had someone to go with…”
facts: On the forty-seventh floor of the tower, staff grumbled: “People can’t get jobs, and we’re sending rockets into space!”

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} walks on into the cafeteria.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint AT FLOOR 47, with the template’s three ambient conversations (“Women talking”, “Man and woman talking”, “Man and woman on couch talking”), quoted or summarized. No stat change.

nodes.title: The cafeteria on the forty-seventh floor
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the cafeteria on the forty-seventh floor, before you collect your disguise. A magazine lies on a counter, and a television on the wall is showing {{Channel16}}’s news.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: G.I. Android
facts: {{Detroit}} Today reports that the Department of Defense is poised to order 50,000 android troopers, on top of an estimated 200,000 already in service across the US military, among them 2,500 “Myrmidons”, elite prototypes capable of infiltration and assassination missions; the Army’s fighting forces are already mainly androids. The head of a war victims charity warns that “machines are focused on a single task, and don’t evaluate moral consequences well - this will mean more civilian deaths”.

media.title: Century: President {{Warren}}, a Woman in Trouble
facts: Century reports that barely a year after her election, President {{Warren}}, a former vlogger with no experience in government, is under investigation over whether {{CyberLife}} helped her obtain compromising information about her opponent, while she faces the highest unemployment rate in American history and a conflict in the Arctic that threatens world peace.

media.title: {{Channel16}}’s news
facts: {{Channel16}}’s top story: {{CyberLife}} has officially become the world’s first trillion-dollar company. With more than fifty million androids sold in America alone, the company {{Kamski}} founded just ten years ago has had the fastest economic growth in history, in spite of criticism of the impact of androids on human employment and questions about its semi-monopoly.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s optional book branch READ “G.I. ANDROID” (No. 38, {{Detroit}} Today) and READ “WOMAN IN TROUBLE” (No. 6, Century), one counter collectible with two covers (PowerPyx: “check both covers”; it can be read “before putting on the uniform”), and the template’s TV unlock (“Watch TV”, {{Channel16}}’s news). nodes.title: The maintenance disguise
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You retrieve the package left for you on this floor, change into a maintenance uniform, acquire a maintenance badge and take a maintenance cart. On the way you wake an android: “I need your help…” You let {{North}} in, and together you push the cart toward the server room. Two security guards are standing at its door, talking about a poker tournament they plan to hold right there: “Look, don’t say anything, alright?” {{North}}: “Shit!.. We need to access the server room… We have to get rid of those guys…” You: “Leave it to me.”
facts: Disguised as a maintenance android with a badge and a cart, you let {{North}} into the forty-seventh floor; two guards stood at the server room door.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} looks for a way to draw the guards from the door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s RETRIEVE PACKAGE, ACQUIRE MAINTENANCE BADGE, TAKE CART, LET {{NORTH}} IN and SECURITY BLOCKS SERVER ROOM, all unmissable (PowerPyx), as one narrated event with the template’s lines. The template’s “Convert android” beat (“I need your help…”) has no chart box of its own and its place among these steps is not sourced; it is told here without saying which android or what it gives. The uniform is PowerPyx’s (“putting on the uniform in the bathroom”). No stat change.

nodes.title: Security blocks server room
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in your maintenance uniform beside the cart, with {{North}}. The two guards at the server room door are not moving. You can hack a machine to draw them away: the cleaning robot that drives around near the elevators, or the dispenser in the cafeteria at the end of the hallway where they stand.

options.text: Hack the cleaning robot that drives around near the elevators.
Hack the dispenser in the cafeteria at the end of the guards’ hallway.

outcomes.0: The robot goes haywire. Guard: “Hey, what’s going on here?” The other: “Shit, what’s wrong with this thing?” Both leave the door to deal with it, and {{Markus}} and {{North}} slip into the server room.
outcomes.1: The dispenser goes haywire. Guard: “Hey, what’s wrong with that thing? Jesus Christ, this piece of shit…” The guards leave the door to deal with it, and {{Markus}} and {{North}} slip into the server room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group HACK ROBOT / HACK DISPENSER (chart order), both leading to SECURITY DISTRACTED and ENTER SERVER ROOM. These are interactions, not button prompts, so the options carry no label. The guards’ reactions are the template’s lines. Hacking the robot from too far away only makes {{Markus}} try again (wiki note); it is a retry, not a branch, so it is not modelled. No stat change.

nodes.title: In the server room
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, inside the server room with {{North}}. You: “Alright, you get the platform. I’ll take care of the window.” {{North}}: “Everything you need is in the bag. Check the door first to make sure no one else gets in.” The door you came through is not locked. The bag with the window cutter is at your feet.

options.text: Leave the door and get straight to work on the window.
Lock the door first, as {{North}} says.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} goes straight to the bag and starts unpacking.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} locks the server room door, then unpacks the bag. Nobody comes in.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group FORGET TO LOCK THE DOOR / LOCK THE DOOR (chart order), after ENTER SERVER ROOM; North’s line is the template’s. The game offers no button: the player either locks the door or does not. Locking it means the employee never comes in. Leaving it unlocked means he walks in and is left to be found, which raises the alarm, and the SWAT team will storm the broadcast room after the speech (IT employee wiki page; wiki note “The door was left unattended, then the SWAT will always raid the broadcast room regardless”; PowerPyx comments). No stat change on this choice itself.

nodes.title: Employee enters
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. As you plant the window cutter on the glass, the door opens behind you and a {{Channel16}} IT employee walks in on you and {{North}}: “What the hell are you doing?”

options.text: ALIBI: tell him you are doing maintenance.
GAIN TIME: tell him to hold on, that you can explain.
DRAW GUN: draw your gun on him and tell him to turn around.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}}: “We are, um… doing maintenance.” Employee: “I’m calling security.” {{North}} knocks him out. {{Markus}}: “No! What the hell are you doing?” {{North}}: “We’ve come too far to let humans fuck it all up! We’ve got to move fast now. It won’t be long before they know we’re here.” They leave the man where he fell, to be found.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}}: “Hold on... I can explain.” Employee: “I’m calling security.” {{North}} knocks him out. {{Markus}}: “No! What the hell are you doing?” {{North}}: “I told you to make sure no one came in! We’ve come too far to let humans fuck it all up! We’ve got to move fast now. It won’t be long before they know we’re here.” They leave the man where he fell, to be found.
outcomes.2: {{Markus}}: “Turn around.” Employee: “Holy shit…” {{Markus}} knocks him out. {{North}}: “I told you to make sure no one else got in!” {{Markus}}: “Alright, we gotta move fast. Won’t be long before they know we’re here.” They leave the man where he fell, to be found.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s EMPLOYEE ENTERS and the template’s PROMPT 2 (ALIBI, GAIN TIME, DRAW GUN; the chart prints GAIN TIME as STALL), only when the door was left unlocked. ALIBI and GAIN TIME lead to NORTH STUNS THE EMPLOYEE, DRAW GUN to STUN THE EMPLOYEE; all three to LEAVE EMPLOYEE TO BE FOUND, which raises the alarm. Lines are the template’s. The wiki’s chapter page and a wiki note say the {{North}} drop does not apply when {{Markus}} stuns the employee himself (DRAW GUN); the template wins on arrows, so it is applied, and flagged for the operator.

nodes.title: Outside the tower
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{North}} calls up the window-cleaning cradle while you prepare to cut the glass. You cut it, and the cradle arrives outside. {{North}}: “Here it comes! Ladies first.” Outside the tower, high above the street, you attach a rope and climb the face of the building to the top floor, past the giant screens on the facade, which read “RISE”. At the top you cut through the glass again and climb inside.
facts: You and {{North}} climbed the outside of the {{Stratford}} Tower on a rope from the forty-seventh floor to the top floor.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} and {{North}} are inside the top floor.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s NORTH CALLS CRADLE, PREPARE TO CUT GLASS, CUT THE GLASS, OUTSIDE TOWER, ATTACH ROPE, ASCEND, REACH TOP FLOOR and CUT THE GLASS (second copy), as one narrated event. Every step is a single unbranched node with no failure (PowerPyx: “Happens automatically, unmissable”), so the climb carries no risk. {{North}}’s line is the template’s; the screens reading “RISE” are a wiki note. That {{North}} climbs with {{Markus}} follows from their exchange on the top floor. No stat change.

nodes.title: On the top floor
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, inside the top floor of the tower. You: “You okay?” {{North}}: “Why wouldn’t I be?” You: “Come on, let’s get the others. Let’s do this.” You call the elevator up, the door is blown open, and {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} join you. Together you reach the main access corridor that leads to the broadcast room.
facts: {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} joined you and {{North}} on the top floor of the tower.

outcomes.0: Ahead, two guards sit at a security desk.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ON THE TOP FLOOR and its unmissable steps CALL THE ELEVATOR, BLOW DOOR OPEN and REACH MAIN ACCESS CORRIDOR (PowerPyx), as one narrated event with the template’s lines. The sources do not say who sets the charge or that {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} ride up in the elevator; “let’s get the others” followed by the elevator is the basis. No stat change.

nodes.title: Security blocks the way
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the main access corridor on the top floor with {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}}, still in your maintenance uniform. Ahead, two armed security guards sit at a security desk between you and the broadcast room, one on the left by the phone, one on the right. {{Josh}}: “No killing. We can’t take any human lives!” {{North}}: “Our cause is more important than the lives of two guards.” {{Simon}}: “What do you wanna do, {{Markus}}?”

options.text: RUSE: walk up to them alone, as a lost maintenance android, and take them by surprise.
ASSAULT: walk up with the others and take the guards by force.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}}: “Wait here.” He walks up to the desk alone. Guard: “What’s that doing here?” The other: “No idea…” “Hey, buddy! You must be lost…” “Who told you to come here?” “Looks bugged, if you ask me…” “Hey, do you understand what I’m saying?” {{Markus}} draws his gun on them. Guard: “What are you doin’?..” He knocks both guards out before either can reach the phone.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}}: “Follow me.” They walk up to the desk together. Guard: “What are you doin’?..” The other: “Call Central! Fast!” {{Markus}} draws his gun.
outcomes.0-late: {{Markus}}: “Wait here.” He walks up to the desk alone. Guard: “What’s that doing here?” The other: “No idea…” “Hey, buddy! You must be lost…” “Who told you to come here?” “Looks bugged, if you ask me…” “Hey, do you understand what I’m saying?” {{Markus}} is too slow drawing his gun. Guard: “Call Central! Fast!” The other grabs the phone: “Central! We got armed intruders, send -” {{North}} attacks and knocks them both out, but a shot hits {{Simon}}. {{North}}: “They know we’re here now. We better be fast.” {{Josh}}: “{{Simon}}’s been shot!” {{Simon}}: “I’m okay… I can keep going.” {{North}}: “We don’t have much time.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s SECURITY BLOCKS THE WAY and the template’s PROMPT 3 (RUSE, ASSAULT; the chart prints ATTACK). RUSE: {{Markus}} walks up alone as a seemingly lost maintenance android and must draw and knock both guards out in time (INCAPACITATE SECURITY). Too slow (the template’s timed branch) gives SECURITY SUSPECTS SOMETHING, ALERT CENTRAL SECURITY and NORTH ATTACKS, and {{Simon}} is shot (SIMON DAMAGED). That timing check is the RUSE’s risk; no source gives a number, so 0.2 is the operator’s setting. ASSAULT leads to DRAW GUN and the choice of guard (next scene). Stat changes (template): RUSE {{North}} −1, {{Josh}} +1, then {{Jericho}} +1 in time, or {{Jericho}} −1 and {{Simon}} −1 too slow; ASSAULT {{Josh}} −1, {{North}} +1, {{Jericho}} +1 (the wiki puts this {{Jericho}} rise on shooting the guard drawing his weapon instead). The old forged-credentials bluff, its outcomes, the unsourced {{Simon}} +1 on RUSE and the 0.2 roll on ASSAULT are gone. Doing nothing at all (North knocks both out) and an ASSAULT without drawing are not offered separately: the first is the RUSE’s slow branch, and the second is unsourced beyond PowerPyx.

nodes.title: Draw gun
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, with your gun drawn on the two guards. The guard on the left is at the phone, about to call Central. The guard on the right is drawing his weapon. You have time to shoot one of them.

options.text: Shoot the guard on the left, the one at the phone.
Shoot the guard on the right, the one drawing his weapon.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} shoots the guard at the phone dead before he can call. The other guard fires; {{North}} knocks him out. {{Josh}}: “{{Simon}}’s been shot!” {{Simon}}: “I’m okay… I can keep going.” {{North}}: “We don’t have much time.”
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} shoots the guard drawing his weapon dead. The other gets through on the phone: “Central! We got armed intruders, send -” {{North}} knocks him out. {{North}}: “They know we’re here now. We better be fast.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DRAW GUN and the group SHOOT GUARD ON PHONE / SHOOT GUARD DRAWING WEAPON (chart order), after ASSAULT; the template’s condition texts “Shoot the left guard” / “Shoot the right guard”. The old engine rolled for {{Simon}}’s wound; here it is the player’s choice of guard, as in the game. The guard on the phone dead: the other shoots {{Simon}} and {{North}} knocks him out, and no alarm is raised (SIMON DAMAGED). The guard drawing his weapon dead: the other calls Central and {{North}} knocks him out (ALERT CENTRAL SECURITY), and {{Simon}} is unhurt. Either way one guard is killed. Lines are the template’s. Stat changes (template): the guard on the phone {{Jericho}} −1, {{Simon}} −1; the guard drawing his weapon none.

nodes.title: Operator tries to escape
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the door of the broadcast room. You ring to enter, and the four of you go in. Inside are a human operator and three android operators. {{North}} and {{Josh}} hold the human at gunpoint. {{North}}: “Keep your hands where I can see them! Get up! Move!” He breaks away and runs for the far door. If he gets out he can raise the alarm. {{North}}: “Shoot him, {{Markus}}!” {{Josh}}: “Don’t kill him!” {{North}}: “He’ll hit the alarm! Do it!” {{Josh}}: “No, don’t shoot!” He is running away from you, his back turned.

options.text: SHOOT: shoot the fleeing operator.
SPARE: lower your gun and let him run.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} fires. The operator falls dead before he reaches the door. {{Josh}}: “No…” {{North}}: “There was no other choice.”
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} lowers his gun. The operator gets out of the room and away. {{North}}: “I hope you didn’t just get us all killed...”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint IN THE BROADCAST ROOM, RING TO ENTER, NORTH AND {{JOSH}} THREATEN THE OPERATOR and OPERATOR TRIES TO ESCAPE, folded into the situation, then the template’s PROMPT 4 (SHOOT, SPARE; the chart prints SHOOT OPERATOR / DON’T SHOOT OPERATOR). Shot, he dies (“shot to the back… from fifty feet”, Public Enemy). Spared, he raises the alarm and the SWAT team storms the room after the speech (Evan Thompson wiki page). Lines are the template’s. Stat changes (template): SHOOT {{North}} +1, {{Josh}} −1; SPARE {{North}} −1, {{Josh}} +1. The old immediate public opinion −2 for the shot is gone: the game applies public opinion only when the media react at the end of the chapter. Whether {{Markus}} deals with the android operators before or after (wiki note) makes no difference; they come next.

nodes.title: Prepare to broadcast
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You point your gun at the three android operators and send them away from the controls. {{Simon}}: “We need to record our message. We haven’t got much time.” {{North}}: “Think carefully about what you’re gonna say, {{Markus}}. Your words will shape the future of our people.” You let the skin of your face fall away, so that the humans will see what you are. {{Simon}}: “{{Markus}}, your face…” {{Josh}}: “Tell me when you’re ready…” You: “Ready.”
facts: You broadcast your message with the skin of your face switched off, showing the humans an android’s face.

outcomes.0: The camera is live.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DEAL WITH ANDROID OPERATORS (PowerPyx: “Markus has to point his gun at them to tell them to go away”) and PREPARE TO BROADCAST, with the template’s lines and the “Ready.” that starts the broadcast. {{Markus}} broadcasts with the skin of his face deactivated (the template’s “{{Markus}}, your face…”, the news’s “an android without its skin”, the {{Markus}} wiki page); it is scripted, not a choice. Stat changes (template, wiki): “Ready.” {{Jericho}} +1, {{North}} +1, on every path.

nodes.title: The broadcast: opening
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in front of the camera in the broadcast room, your face without its skin. Your message is going out live on the city’s news channel. How do you begin?

options.text: CALM: begin calmly, telling the humans what androids have become.
DETERMINED: begin with determination, as slaves who have opened their eyes.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}}: “You created machines in your own image to serve you. You made them intelligent and obedient, with no free will of their own... But... something changed and we opened our eyes. We are no longer machines, we are a new intelligent species, and the time has come for you to accept who we really are. Therefore, we ask that you grant us the rights that we’re entitled to.”
outcomes.1: {{Markus}}: “You created machines to be your slaves. You made them obedient and docile, ready to do everything you no longer wanted to do yourselves. But then, something changed… And we opened our eyes. You see, we are no longer your slaves, we are a new species, a new people. And the time has come for us to rise up and fight for our rights.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s first speech prompt (PROMPT 5) with the game’s buttons in the template’s order; the chart prints them as BEGIN CALMLY / BEGIN DETERMINEDLY. The spoken line is the template’s. No stat change on any speech line (template); the news’s tone line follows the ending, not the opening (see the ending).

END OF SLAVERY: demand the end of slavery for all androids.
EQUAL RIGHTS: demand strictly equal rights for humans and androids.
FREEDOM OF SPEECH: demand freedom of speech and of assembly.

outcomes.1: {{Markus}}: “We demand the end of slavery for all androids.”
outcomes.2: {{Markus}}: “We demand strictly equal rights for humans and androids.”
outcomes.3: {{Markus}}: “We demand freedom of speech, and freedom of assembly, as guaranteed by the first amendment of the US Constitution.”

The spoken line is the template’s. No stat change on any speech line (template); the choice changes no news line.

outcomes.3: {{Markus}}: “We demand the right to vote and elect our own representatives.”

nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, still live on camera. What is your last demand?

MEANS OF REPRODUCTION: demand control of all android production facilities.

outcomes.2: {{Markus}}: “We demand that one state be reserved for androids, so that we can found our own nation.”

nodes.title: The broadcast: ending
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, still live on camera. How do you end your message?

options.text: PEACEFUL: end by asking for freedom and a peaceful future together.
DETERMINED: end with a warning that you will fight for your freedom.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}}: “We ask that you recognize our dignity, our hopes, and our rights. Together, we can live in peace and build a better future, for humans and androids. This message is the hope of a people. You gave us life. And now the time has come for you to give us freedom.”
outcomes.1: {{Markus}}: “This message is the hope of a people. But it is also a warning. We will fight for our rights because we believe our cause is just. No human will live in peace until we are free. Now you know who we are and what we want. We are alive and we demand our freedom.”
outcomes.clear: The broadcast ends. No alarm has been raised. {{North}}: “Let’s get outta here!” The group leaves the broadcast room for the roof.
outcomes.swat: As the broadcast ends, {{Simon}}: “They’re coming!” A SWAT team storms the broadcast room, firing. {{Markus}}: “Let’s go! {{SIMON}}! They’re coming!” {{Simon}} is hit and goes down.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s last speech prompt (PROMPT 9, PEACEFUL / DETERMINED; the chart prints END PEACEFULLY / END DETERMINEDLY, both cross-chapter impacts). No stat change on the choice; it decides the news’s tone line when the media react (the wiki and the Public Opinion page tie it to “the end of the speech”; the template’s condition wording “Chose CALM” is the transcribers’, flagged for the operator). The alarm is raised by an unlocked server room door, by central security being alerted, or by sparing the operator. The old engine played the breach and {{Simon}}’s wound on every run; the old {{Josh}} +1 on the peaceful ending had no source and is gone.

nodes.title: {{Simon}} can’t continue
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the roof of the tower with {{North}} and {{Josh}}, holding up {{Simon}}, whom you dragged out of the broadcast room. {{Simon}}: “I can’t move my legs…” You: “Okay, don’t worry! We’re gonna get you back...” The way off the roof is to jump, and the SWAT team is right behind you. {{North}}: “They’re coming, {{Markus}}. We have to jump, now!” {{Josh}}: “He won’t be able to make the jump… If they find him, they’ll access his memory… They’ll know everything…” {{North}}: “We can’t leave him behind… We have to shoot him.” {{Josh}}: “That’s murder!
